tpl.review.label: Review changes
tpl.tests.label: Write tests
tpl.tests.description: Write tests for a file or function
tpl.tests.body:
Write tests for: $ARGUMENTS

- Use the test framework and style the project already uses (look at existing tests).
- Cover the main path, edge cases, and errors.
- Don't change the code under test unless you have to; if you find a bug, report it separately.
- Run the tests and make sure they pass.
tpl.explain.label: Explain a file
tpl.explain.body:
Explain how the file $ARGUMENTS works.

- What it's for and where it's used.
- The main functions/classes and how they fit together.
- Non-obvious parts and possible pitfalls.

Keep it brief and reference line numbers.
tpl.commit-msg.label: Commit message
tpl.commit-msg.description: Suggest a commit message for the staged changes
tpl.commit-msg.body:
Look at the staged changes (`git diff --cached`; if empty, `git diff`) and the recent commits (`git log -10 --oneline`) to match the existing style.

Suggest a commit message: a short subject line under 72 characters and, if needed, a body explaining why. Don't make the commit yourself.
tpl.blank-cmd.label: Blank command
tpl.blank-cmd.body: Describe the task for Claude. $ARGUMENTS is everything typed after the command name; $1, $2… are individual arguments.
tpl.skill-blank.label: Blank skill
tpl.skill-blank.body:
# Skill name

## When to use
Describe the situations in which Claude should apply this skill.

## Instructions
1. First step.
2. Second step.

## Examples
- An example request and the expected result.
tpl.skill-style.label: Project code style
tpl.skill-style.description: Code style rules for this project. Use when writing or editing code in this repository.
tpl.skill-style.body:
# Code style

## General rules
- Follow the formatting already used in the file (indentation, quotes, semicolons).
- Use descriptive names; no abbreviations except common ones.
- Comments explain why, not what.

## Before finishing
- Run the linter and tests if the project has them.
